name: Fluence
tagline: Speak off the cuff, get honest coaching on how you actually spoke.
description:
Fluence is a spontaneous-speech coach that lives in a GIF.

Pick a drill — freestyle, or one of nine types from the catalog — and record a take. GifOS captures the clip behind its own visible recorder, so the app never holds the live microphone. Deepgram nova-3 returns a transcript with per-word timestamps, confidence and filler tagging; a pure-JavaScript pass then extracts the honest, comparable signal: pace and articulation rate, pauses and long-pause moments, fillers, hedges, adjacent-repeat restarts, lexical diversity and vocabulary reach, ASR confidence and sentence structure.

Only then does a language model weigh in, with drill-type-aware grading rules — a listing task is graded on item count, a narrative on structure. You get evidence-grounded coaching that quotes what you said, a suggested next drill aimed at your top weakness, and a weekly review that tracks whether any of it is working. Picture-description drills draw their own scene.

Every take, review and benchmark stays private, inside the icon on your Home Screen.
